category_title: Middle school students with LD exhibiting low engagement and poor material management
minimal_context: Chris is sitting in his 50-minute math class with the goal of acquiring new math concepts.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Chris, it is time to start our 50-minute math class. Please get out your pencil, paper, and math book so we can begin.

STUDENT: (Drawing pictures) I don't have my pencil, paper, or math book today.

TUTOR: You need to stop drawing and pay attention to the lesson.

STUDENT: Math is just not my subject. Watch this, I'm going to draw something funny to show the other students.

TUTOR: Please look up here at the board and try to follow along with the concepts.

STUDENT: (Continues doodling, not looking at the teacher) I know that when I listen more I get it more easily, but I'm just going to keep drawing.

options.A: Develop critical consciousness through genuine multicultural math curricula addressing authentic issues of race, ethnicity, social class, and disability from various positionalities.
options.B: Provide the student with access to similar, but more socially appropriate, sensory stimulation during math class by giving him a squishy stress-relief ball.
options.C: Synthesize baseline data and collaboratively set a goal with the student to improve math performance by targeting preparedness to learn and on-task behavior.
options.D: Provide continuous, increasing amounts of math work to the student throughout the 50-minute class period.
